item.title: Yasaka Shrine: Gion's Lantern-Lit Guardian Shrine — Guide
item.description: Yasaka Shrine, sometimes called Gion-san, sits at the eastern end of Shijo street where it meets the Gion district and the slopes of Higashiyama. Founded over 1,300 years ago, it is one of Kyoto’s most popular shrines, its bright vermilion gate and main hall always open and free to enter, day or night. After dark its central dance stage glows with hundreds of paper lanterns donated by local businesses, and its grounds flow directly into Maruyama Park behind.

item.title: Kasuga Taisha: The Lantern Shrine in the Sacred Forest — Guide
item.description: Kasuga Taisha, founded in 768 as the tutelary shrine of the powerful Fujiwara clan, is one of Nara’s most atmospheric sites: a vivid vermilion shrine set deep within the Kasugayama primeval forest, reached along a wooded approach lined with some 2,000 moss-covered stone lanterns. Inside, around a thousand bronze lanterns hang from the eaves, and twice a year — at Setsubun in February and Obon in August — all 3,000 are lit at once for the Mantoro festival, filling the shrine with flickering gold.
